front.title: Extend-Only, Threshold-Attested Authority Renewal for Partitioned Agent Meshes

abstract.t: Every workload identity architecture in deployment today assumes its credential issuer is reachable: short-lived tokens, fast rotation and timely revocation are guarantees about the connected case. This document specifies what a workload does when that assumption fails, when its credential is nearing or past expiry and its issuer cannot be reached. It defines extend-only, threshold-attested authority renewal. Before any partition, the issuer signs a Mesh Manifest that appoints a bounded set of peers as a limited-authority local issuer: it names the members, fixes a ceiling on total extension, caps the scope any renewal may carry, and sets a validity window. During a partition, a severed workload broadcasts a signed renewal request to those peers; each peer independently verifies that the request extends existing authority without widening it, within the manifest's ceiling, and against its own first-hand observation of the requester's health; each attestation signs the digest of the entire request, so scope, requester, timestamps and predecessor are all under the peer's signature; once a two-thirds threshold of the peers (ceil(2N/3) of N >= 4) has attested, the workload treats its authority as extended through a bounded expiry. Rounds are hash- linked, so a chain's signatures commit to the exact history being extended. The document specifies the manifest, the message formats, the independent-evaluation procedure, the renewal-chain construction for partitions outlasting one round, and the verification procedure a relying party runs given the manifest, the chain and the original credential it already trusts. It also specifies, normatively, what this mechanism does not provide: it is not a consensus protocol, it does not establish that a workload is uncompromised, and a revocation issued during a partition is not enforceable until the partition heals; an implementation MUST NOT represent this mechanism as providing partition-proof revocation.
